intro.title: prefers-reduced-motion
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a spinning animation and learn how to respect user preferences for reduced motion. You will use the CSS `prefers-reduced-motion` media query to detect if a user has requested less animation on their device. The core concept is applying conditional styles based on system settings, using keyframes for animation and media queries for control. This involves writing CSS rules that toggle or modify animations when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active. By the end, you'll create a page that spins an element smoothly by default but stops or slows the spin for users who prefer reduced motion.
intro.usecase: The `prefers-reduced-motion` media query is essential for building accessible web applications that respect user preferences. In real-world products like admin dashboards with animated charts, e-commerce sites with carousels, or news apps with auto-scrolling feeds, developers use it to disable or simplify animations for users who experience motion sickness or vestibular disorders. This ensures compliance with accessibility standards (WCAG) and improves the user experience for a significant portion of the audience. Implementing it involves conditionally applying CSS rules to reduce or remove motion-based effects while maintaining core functionality.
